title: Pack for the first thing you need
hook: The rain jacket is under five items. How many do you lift to reach it?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that in a bag opened from the top you must lift everything above an item to reach it, so the item needed first should go in last

misconception: Packing order doesn't matter as long as everything fits in the bag.
objective: Every item above the one you need has to come out first. With the jacket on top, nothing is in the way, so the thing you need first is best packed last.

recall.question: A top-opening bag holds 8 layers, and the item you need first is at the bottom. How many layers must you lift out, and how many if it had been packed on top?
recall.why: With top access, a bottom item has N − 1 = 7 layers above it; on top, it has 0. The bag fits the same either way; access does not. Pockets and side openings change the count.
